---
title: "The look"
---


The layout you are reading: a centred grid of at most 76rem, three
columns on wide screens — navigation, content, table of contents. The
header stays pinned while you scroll, and content disappears behind it
as behind frosted glass rather than a hard edge. All of it lives in one
rules file, `_extensions/easyqda-theme/easyqda.scss`; the two palette
files contribute colours and nothing else.

## The header

Left to right: an open-book glyph before the site title (a placeholder
that [a logo can replace](customising.qmd)), then — at the right edge of
the content column — search, the PDF icon, the language menu and the
day/night toggle. The GitHub link sits apart from them, above the right
sidebar, where a reader's eye expects the way out to the source.

The toggle shows a moon in light mode and a sun in dark mode. The
language menu is a dropdown rather than a two-way switch, so sites are
not locked in when a third language arrives.

## The sidebars

Navigation entries are set slightly larger than Quarto's default, with
more air between them — long section lists stay scannable. The current
page carries a soft accent pill that extends a little beyond its text,
the same visual language the zotQDA plugin documentation always had.
The right column highlights the section you are reading as you scroll;
that scrollspy is one of the things the
[offline repairs](offline.qmd) keep working from a plain file tree.

## Callouts

Quarto's native callouts, restyled to match:

::: {.callout-note title="A note"}
Written as `::: {.callout-note}` — nothing theme-specific to learn.
The five Quarto types (`note`, `tip`, `warning`, `important`,
`caution`) all render.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="A warning"}
The zotQDA sites use these for their beta notices.
:::

## Code and type

Text is self-hosted Noto Sans — chosen for its wide Unicode coverage,
which matters in scientific writing (α, ≤, →, combining diacritics all
render from the same family). Code blocks highlight with `github` in
light mode and `github-dark` in dark mode:

```python
def alpha(do, de):
    """Krippendorff, in one line."""
    return 1 - do / de
```

Both palettes, the pill, the frosted header and the sidebar type are
inspectable on this very page — switch the toggle in the header and
watch the whole page follow, code blocks included.
